sub_palette: near_eastern (akkadian) lean + east_asian (japonic) substrate (cross-family fusion, Mesopotamian-leaning)

blend.lean_parent: near_eastern (akkadian: the alu/bit temple-cities, the sangu priesthood, construct-chain toponyms, emphatic gutturals, -u/-um endings, SOV agglutinative grammar, penultimate stress)
blend.substrate_parent: east_asian (japonic: the open CV-mora islands and shrine-isles, the kami of mountain and sea, the rice-and-silk staple words, the torii and the castle-town)
blend.lean: Near-Eastern-heavy (Akkadian) - a single fused people of the temple-isles, where the ziggurat-priesthood of the Two Rivers and the shrine-kami of the island-arc grew into one tongue and one rite. The Akkadian temple-and-rule register is the backbone; the Japonic island/shrine/material words are the substrate. Not a ruling elite over a populace - one merged people, one fused language (per gdd-hybrid-conlang-fusion.md).

_note: NEW cross-family hybrid under the base/hybrid model. BASE_03 Shinarur (Mesopotamian) x BASE_08 (Japonic). FUSION-FIRST (gdd-hybrid-conlang-fusion.md): a SINGLE fused tongue, one word per concept, derived by principled sound-change from both parents - not a slash-pair dual-register gloss. CIV/CLAN DECIDED by inheritance: Mesopotamian base = Civilized, Japonic base = Clanhold, and any Civ parent -> Civ, so Hinoshinar is Civilized (feudal). Concept: the temple-city and the shrine-isle as one - ziggurat and torii, the sangu-priest and the kannushi grown into a single rite over the river-cities of an island-arc. Lean = Akkadian (the rule/temple/kin/land register, the construct-chain toponyms, the -u/-um endings); substrate = Japonic (island, shrine, mountain, sea, rice, silk, jade - the land and material words). Common-word lexicon and rank titles use the real Akkadian register (allowed, catalog 5.3), with the Japonic substrate words fused into Akkadian phonology; DEITY names are morphs of the Agrippan canon - Akkadian canon-morphs PRIMARY (the hammuran column), Japonic kami-morphs SECONDARY (the yamataian/family_east_asian.json japonic column), never real Mesopotamian gods or Shinto kami. All three alignments (per 2026-06-27: all human cultures allow Lawful/Neutral/Chaotic). Ruler/domain DISPLAY titles are ENGLISH (Mesopotamian-led; no approved foreign term required); conlang titles in ruler_native/domain_native (Akkadian) for NPC dialogue. The duchy display is set to 'Daimyo' as an apt, commonly-known term for the great island-house lord beneath the throne (see display_policy).

phonology.palette: Near-Eastern (Akkadian) lean - emphatic and guttural consonants (q, kh, h, ', sh, ts), triconsonantal roots, a/i/u vowels, -u/-um/-tu endings, penultimate stress, CVC syllables and construct chains - taking up an East-Asian (Japonic) substrate: open CV moras, the five vowels a i u e o, the island/shrine/mountain/sea/rice/silk word-stock, rendaku voicing. Per the CSV: soft consonants with deep vowels (the Japonic CV gentleness audible beneath the Akkadian emphatics and -u/-um closes); grammar is SOV with agglutinative particles and suffixes (both parents agree - Akkadian agglutinative case carried over Japonic-derived -no linking, reshaped to Akkadian CVC). Theophoric on the Akkadian canon-morphs (Tullaru-, Urlandu-) with the Japonic kami-morphs as the shrine register (Terashu-, Haganu-).
phonology.phonotactics: CVC dominant (Akkadian); Japonic CV-mora roots take Akkadian -u/-um/-tu closes and shed final open vowels or harden them to a consonant-final stem; construct chains and mimation -um; stress penultimate (the Akkadian pull overrides Japonic pitch-accent); Bit-/Dur-/Kar- construct toponyms over -shu/-yamu island-and-shrine elements.

sound_changes: Japonic open CV-moras collapse into Akkadian CVC: final open vowel drops or the stem hardens consonant-final, then takes an Akkadian -u/-um/-tu nominal close (yama>yamu, shima>shimu, mori>muru, umi>umu)
Japonic plain stops sharpen toward Akkadian emphatics/gutturals: k>k/q, t>t/ts, s>sh before high vowels, voiced g/d/b retained; geminates from rendaku resolve to single emphatics
Japonic pitch-accent is overridden by Akkadian penultimate stress on every word; the Japonic -no linking particle is kept agglutinatively but reduced (X-no-Y > X-nu-)

Akkadian -u/-i/-a vowel triad dominates; Japonic e/o are admitted only in stressed substrate roots, else raised (e>i, o>u); retain Akkadian sh, q, ', kh and the Japonic open-vowel color of substrate stems
very short Japonic roots take an Akkadian -u/-um ending to reach a CVC(u) shape (ko>kuru, no>nuru, do>duru)
fusion_rules.source_tilt: island/shrine/mountain/sea/coast/material/staple words from Japonic roots (the substrate land and its making - shima, yama, umi, jinja, kome, kinu, hisui), then filtered to Akkadian phonology; kin-line/rule/temple/land/quality/abstract/war words from Akkadian roots (the lean register - mar, bit, alu, naru, rabu, ellu); every chosen root then run through the one Akkadian-shaped sound-law so the split is invisible at the surface

lexicon._note: Single fused tongue derived via phonology.fusion_rules (gdd-hybrid-conlang-fusion.md): Japonic island/shrine/material/staple roots + Akkadian rule/kin/temple/land roots, all run through one Akkadian-shaped sound-law (CV-moras hardened to CVC with -u/-um closes, penultimate stress); portmanteaus mark the blended institutions and bloodline. One word per concept, no slashes.

morphology.patronymic_form: the Akkadian 'mar-' (son of) patronymic and theophoric constructs are the lead form; the Japonic substrate keeps a reduced clan-linking -nu- (from -no-) before the given name; nobility carry a Bit- house-name. The throne fuses both - a sharru who also heads an island Bit- house with a -nu- shrine-lineage.
morphology.compounding_rule: Akkadian construct-chains (Bit-[god], Dur-[ruler], Kar-[god]) layered over fused feature-compounds (quality + island/shrine element): the capital Hinoshinar (the temple-isle, hino + shinar), Dur-Tullaru (fort of Tullaru), Kuru-yamu (black-mountain), Aka-shirkallu (the red citadel).

title_ladder.government: feudal (a fused temple-and-isle realm: the sharru and his rubu-kin at the crown over the Tenka-isles, the shaknu-governors over the alu river-cities, the great island-houses - the daimyo of the shrine-isles - sworn beneath; the sangu-priesthood and the kannushi-shrine-keepers serve the rite together)
title_ladder._tiers_note: Akkadian ladder, ascending, -u/-utu rhyme (Hazannu/Hazannutu ... Sharru/Sharrutu). Hazannu (mayor) barony; Massaru (warden) march; Shaknu (appointed governor) county; Turtanu (commander-in-chief) duchy; Rubu (prince) principality; Sharru (king) kingdom over a Sharrutu; Shar-kishshati (king of the totality) empire over the Kishshatu. DISPLAY titles are English; the duchy display is set to 'Daimyo' as the apt, commonly-known term for the great island-house lord (the Japonic-substrate co-rank), its native Akkadian form remaining Turtanu. The Japonic substrate keeps its shugo-governor and kannushi-priest beneath the Akkadian crown; the gudja-equivalent sangu and the scribal shatammu stand outside the ladder. Rank native-forms use the real Akkadian register (allowed).
title_ladder.heir: Mar-Sharri (son of the king; the crown heir)

honorifics.champion: Redu (Akkadian soldier) / Bushu (the warrior, from Japonic bushi)

vassalage.tribute: Biltu / Nengu (the isle-render, from Japonic nengu)

title_ladder.display_policy: Ruler/domain titles shown in setting-gen, domain lists and vassal trees are ENGLISH, except the duchy which uses the approved commonly-known term 'Daimyo' (the great island-house lord). The *_native conlang (Akkadian) forms are for NPC DIALOGUE ONLY, never for structural/UI displays.

people_name_convention.order: given (often theophoric) + Akkadian mar- patronymic or Bit- house; the Japonic-substrate folk add a reduced -nu- shrine-lineage before the given name; order given-first (the Akkadian lean overrides the Japonic family-first order).
people_name_convention.dual_register: the temple-and-rule register carries Akkadian theophoric names (X-iddina, Warad-X) on the morphed canon-stems; the island-shrine substrate carries fused given names on the kami-morphs (Terashu-, Haganu-) with -maru/-himu endings hardened to the lean phonology.
people_name_convention.theophoric: Akkadian devotional constructs lead: Warad-Tullaru (servant of Tullaru), Tullaru-iddina (Tullaru-gave-me); the shrine register builds on the Japonic kami-morphs: Terashu-bani (Terashu-made), Haganu-musmaru (son of Haganu).

religion._note: Deity-names are morphs of the Agrippan canon - Akkadian canon-morphs PRIMARY (family_near_eastern / hammuran, the akkadian column), Japonic kami-morphs SECONDARY (family_east_asian.json theonym_sets.japonic, the yamataian column), never real Mesopotamian gods or Shinto kami. The fused rite identifies the temple-power and the shrine-kami as one face: the sangu of the ziggurat and the kannushi of the torii keep the same powers. All three alignments.
religion.the_one: Itarnu (Akkadian; Jp shrine-name Takamu-no-kami) - the distant Ancient One, honored not petitioned

sample_deity_renames.Tulrius: Tullaru (Jp Terashu) - the sun and judgment
sample_deity_renames.Gaiandus: Gayandu (Jp Iwanu) - the enduring earth and mountain

worship_by_alignment.Lawful: venerates the Lawful powers - Itarnu, Tullaru the just, Urlandu of the sworn oath, Rialtu the merciful - at the ziggurat and the torii-grove alike, and names the Chaotic powers lemnu (evil) or aramitama (the wild spirits), warded; the law-stele and the kami-rite bind together
worship_by_alignment.Neutral: the ancestral dead (the senzabu inscribed on the temple-stele and enshrined at the household jinbitu) and the city-and-isle spirits of the bit-ili and the shrine-isles; the great powers invoked at temple and torii situationally
worship_by_alignment.Chaotic: Venerates the Chaotic powers of the canon - the war-flame and the devouring void, the storm-kami and the mountain-oni - and names the Lawful powers, and Itarnu, as the tyrant-powers to be defied.

religion.demon_epithet_pattern: the Chaotic powers, warded as -lemnu (Akkadian evil) or aramitama (Japonic wild spirits), keep their morphs + an epithet: Maraxus -> Marakshu the City-Burner (Jp Takebu the War-Flame); Vacidus -> Bakidu-lemnu the Unmaking (Jp Utsuru the Devouring Void); Lusanto -> Lusantu the Hoard-Worm (Jp Koganu-Orochu the gold serpent).

clergy_ladder.9: Shatammu (temple-primate) / Saishu (high priest of the realm)

religion.religious_orders_pattern: the Bit-ili (god-house/temple) or the Jinbitu (shrine-isle temple) of [power]: 'the Bit-ili of Tullaru', 'the Jinbitu of Terashu', within its ziggurat-court and torii-grove.
religion.saints_pattern: the deified law-givers and heroes inscribed on the temple-stele, and the great ancestors enshrined as kami at the isle-jinbitu (the honored dead); 'the Just [name]', 'the kami [name]'.

holy_symbol_motifs.Urlandu: an iron blade crossed before a torii and the city-standard
holy_symbol_motifs.Gayandu: the alluvial field and the island-mountain beneath the ziggurat
